grade.first_issue: The assertion that every open interval of length at least \(\theta\) contains a multiple of \(\theta\) is false when its length is exactly \(\theta\) and both endpoints are consecutive multiples. Here the only relevant exception is \(k=3\) with an equilateral triangle, which is already terminal and should be handled separately.
grade.summary: The submitted solution gives the correct characterization and essentially valid strategies in both directions. The sufficiency argument has a minor endpoint oversight, while the necessity argument correctly establishes the invariant that every cut of a triangle avoiding all positive multiples of \(\theta\) has a child with the same property. The existence of an initial such triangle is asserted rather than exhibited, but is repaired immediately by choosing the equilateral triangle.
strengths: Correctly identifies all and only \(\theta=180^\circ/k\) with integers \(k\ge2\).
Gives a valid induction reducing an angle \(n\theta\) to \(\theta\).
The four-case analysis in the necessity direction correctly proves the safe-triangle invariant.

errors.description: The open-interval multiple claim overlooks its equality endpoint case; the exceptional triangle is already winning.
The existence of an initial triangle avoiding \(W\) is asserted without justification, though \((60^\circ,60^\circ,60^\circ)\) works immediately under the stated assumption.
